findings.title: Remove the remaining attribution of a quantitative determinant bound to RandomMatrices
findings.finding: The statement still says that the supplier’s determinant-continuity bound gives a uniform estimate. The audited RandomMatrices §8.3 contract states trace-norm continuity, not that quantitative bound. The new UniformDeterminant supporting construction correctly proves uniform convergence from compactness of K0(K) and continuity; the main sentence contradicts that dependency boundary.
findings.replacement_en: For each compact parameter set K, the image K₀(K) is compact in trace norm. Apply continuity of the generic determinant at the points of that compact image and a finite subcover; compact-uniform trace-norm convergence then gives uniform scalar convergence on K. The holomorphic-family assertion is proved from normal convergence of the exterior-power series with the trace-norm estimates constructed here.
findings.replacement_ja: 各コンパクトなパラメータ集合 K に対し、像 K₀(K) はトレースノルムでコンパクトである。この像の各点での一般行列式の連続性と有限部分被覆を用い、K 上のトレースノルム一様収束からスカラー行列式の一様収束を得る。正則な族に関する主張は、ここで構成するトレースノルム評価と外冪級数の正規収束から証明する。
findings.preservation: Keeps the same determinant, holomorphy, convergence and zero-count targets; removes only the unsupported supplier attribution.

findings.title: Construct a determinant-frame differential for every Fredholm chart before specializing to a trace-class formula
findings.finding: P8.2 constructs a holomorphic index-zero Fredholm family, but no general theorem makes that original operator I−K with K trace class. P8.3 API3 and P8.4 then promise the displayed trace-class logarithmic derivative on every constructed ramified/resonant chart. A1.1 supplies a finite-dimensional stabilization representation, which resolves this gap without weakening the normalization scope.
findings.diagnostic: On an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, T_s=e^s I is a holomorphic invertible Fredholm family. T_s⁻¹dT_s=I ds has no trace-class trace. A determinant-line construction exists nonetheless. Thus a general Fredholm family alone does not justify the unrestricted infinite-dimensional trace formula.
findings.replacement_en: On each A1.1 stabilization chart, choose holomorphic frames for the equal-rank bundles K_stab and F and let S(s) represent the projection K_stab→F. The canonical section has representative det S. Prove d log(det S)=Tr(S⁻¹dS) on its nonvanishing locus and the actual logarithmic correction for a change of determinant frame. This gives the determinant-frame form and scalar normalization on every constructed RHP chart, including the ramified and resonant adapters. Equivalently, K_fin=I−S on the finite-dimensional space F gives the displayed trace-class identity. For a claimed infinite-dimensional integrable-kernel realization K, additionally construct its trace-norm holomorphic family and the comparison τ=u det(I−K), with u nowhere zero; only then use d log τ=d log u−Tr((I−K)⁻¹dK). The JMU/Hamiltonian comparison retains its stated generic locus.
findings.replacement_ja: A1.1 の各安定化チャートで、同じ階数の束 K_stab と F の正則フレームを選び、射影 K_stab→F を表す行列を S(s) とする。標準切断の代表は det S である。非消滅領域で d log(det S)=Tr(S⁻¹dS) を証明し、行列式フレームの変更に伴う実際の対数補正を証明する。これにより分岐・共鳴のアダプターを含む全ての構成済み RHP チャートで行列式フレームの1形式とスカラー正規化を得る。同値に、有限次元空間 F 上で K_fin=I−S と置けば、表示したトレースクラス恒等式を得る。無限次元の可積分核 K による実現を主張する場合は、トレースノルムで正則な族と、非消滅因子 u を伴う τ=u det(I−K) の比較を構成した上で d log τ=d log u−Tr((I−K)⁻¹dK) を用いる。JMU/Hamiltonian 比較の一般領域に関する仮定は保持する。
findings.preservation: Keeps every retained RHP stratum, determinant section, divisor, normalization and all verified trace-class/JMU comparisons. It supplies the missing universal local construction rather than assuming a universal infinite-dimensional realization.
evidence: R1 A1.6 explicitly says not every RHP is assumed trace-class representable

findings.title: Localize the Picard smoothness obstruction test to affine square-zero bases
findings.finding: The arbitrary quasi-coherent square-zero ideal is a correct improvement over finite-dimensional complex kernels. The paragraph still asks for a cohomological-dimension vanishing on proper relative curves without saying that the test base is affine. Relative dimension at most one gives R^q p_*J=0 for q>1, not H²(C_T0,J)=0 over arbitrary nonaffine T0. The latter is the obstruction group needed in the displayed lifting argument.
findings.diagnostic: Take T₀ to be an abelian surface, C_T0=P¹×T₀, and a trivial square-zero thickening with ideal O_T0. Then H²(C_T0,p*O_T0)=H²(T₀,O_T0) is nonzero, although every curve fiber has H²=0. Formal smoothness is still proved by local affine tests and descent.
findings.replacement_en: Test formal smoothness locally on affine square-zero thickenings T₀↪T with quasi-coherent ideal I. Flatness identifies the ideal of C_T0 in C_T with p*I. Construct the obstruction in H²(C_T0,p*I), the torsor of isomorphism classes of lifts with a specified restriction isomorphism under H¹(C_T0,p*I), and their infinitesimal automorphisms from H⁰. Prove R^q p_*(p*I)=0 for q>1 by proper relative dimension at most one and use the affine base and Leray to obtain H²=0. Handle general test bases by open/fppf descent and apply the local finite-presentation criterion to deduce smoothness. Do not infer absolute H² vanishing on a nonaffine base from fiber dimension.
findings.replacement_ja: 形式的滑らかさは、準連接イデアル I を持つ affine な平方零肥厚 T₀↪T に局所化して検証する。平坦性により C_T 内の C_T0 のイデアルを p*I と同定する。H²(C_T0,p*I) に値を取る障害、制限同型を指定した持上げの同型類に対する H¹(C_T0,p*I) の torsor、および H⁰ から得る微小自己同型を構成する。固有かつ相対次元が高々1であることから q>1 で R^q p_*(p*I)=0 を証明し、基底の affine 性と Leray により H²=0 を得る。一般の試験基底は開被覆または fppf 降下で扱い、局所有限表示の判定から滑らかさを導く。非 affine 基底上の絶対 H² 消滅をファイバー次元だけから推論しない。
findings.preservation: Keeps the full relative Picard result, nonreduced curves and bases, and arbitrary square-zero ideal scope; specifies the valid local proof mechanism.

findings.title: Name the analytic-space carrier consumed by the complex analytic branch
findings.finding: C1.2 allows a complex analytic base and arbitrary base change, but its declared suppliers are algebraic vector bundles, algebraic cohomology and smooth real Poisson theory. The complex analytic category retaining nilpotents is owned by the foundational prefix of M1.2. Naming that shared carrier closes the ownership graph; there is no need to assume connection-moduli conclusions.
findings.replacement_en: For the analytic branch, use the complex analytic-space and coherent/finite locally free sheaf carriers constructed in the analytic foundational prefix of M1.2, retaining nilpotent coefficients. Construct the relative vector-bundle and unit-group charts by local trivializations and prove their gluing and base-change comparisons. C1.2 owns the relative complex Poisson, coadjoint, residue and conditional reduction comparisons. This use of shared carriers imports no connection-moduli, RH or Painlevé theorem.

positive_checks: A1.1 uses native complex Fredholm/stabilization and the dual determinant convention; it explicitly excludes pointwise treatment of nilpotent bases.
A1.2 owns weighted cross-branch Schur estimates; the endpoint essential-singularity example has the stated L² norm squared exp(−2)/2.
A1.3’s constant −I₂ jump is a valid nonsmall but solvable example; A1.4’s translated Gaussian has the stated nonzero asymptotic remainder factor (1−i)/2.

C1.1’s exact finite rational identity, highest coefficient, insufficient scaling and nonlinear-parameter correction are mathematically consistent; C1.2’s dual/Frobenius distinction and negation sign are retained.
P8 keeps odd-degree index-zero normalization and acyclic comparison restrictions; the new concern is the missing local finite-dimensional versus infinite-dimensional trace distinction.
P9’s PI sigma affine spurious branch and PII sigma loss of phase data are valid diagnostics; the Flaschka–Newell/P34 to PII inversion carries its required U≠0 restriction.

P10.3’s quantitative sector estimates match ILP18 (4.74); the angular estimates yield the stated first and second arc orders, and calibration +iπ/24 matches (4.76). This is a verification of the specified target and source scope, not a proof of the required uniform parametrices.
P11’s nilpotent and semisimple collision examples have distinct projective slopes despite the same divisor; the determinant trace test correctly excludes the extra scalar irregular endpoint.

M1.2.GF03a now separates proper relative higher-direct-image comparison from absolute proper GAGA. The relative-proper identity map A¹→A¹ would not justify full coherent GAGA; R1 no longer claims that.

M2.2.RelativeLinearity retains p⁻¹O_B-linearity and correctly avoids treating the connection differential as O_C-linear. Moving framed versal comparison into M2.2 avoids using it to assume the earlier GIT construction.

GF01–GF13 retain field versus family formal decomposition, actual reductive GIT stages, finite-inertia restrictions, full resonant logarithmic lattices, exact I13 properness scope and first-boundary-layer versus all-supported-cohomology distinctions.

No additional English/Japanese formula, parameter-domain or counterexample mismatch was found in the reviewed A/C/P7–P11 and relative-linearity/Picard passages. The reported defects occur in both languages, apart from the remaining English optional appendix wording.
